summary: Bamboo is a dense action-selection and tile-optimization game where you place bamboo tiles onto a shared board to trigger effects, then spend those resources on personal home-tile puzzles for balance, cooking, and finance. It plays like a lighter cousin of Bitoku, with tight turn order tension over which spots on the shared board get taken and a heavy focus on optimizing your own tableau over four years of seasonal turns.
praised: Satisfying puzzle of optimizing home tiles and balance patterns
Good production and thematic art consistent with the Kemushi series
Meaningful tension over shared board spaces without being overly confrontational
Strong sense of progression across the four game-years
criticised: Rulebook and icon-heavy symbology can be a steep initial learning curve
Some player-count and turn-order imbalance, especially at higher player counts
Can feel a bit dry or overly mechanical/soulless despite the theme
Runtime feels long relative to the depth of decisions for some players

interaction.kind: blocking and area denial over shared action/board spaces, otherwise mostly parallel optimization

scoring.why: Final score is an accumulation across several home-tile categories (balance, cooking, finance, home improvement) plus bonuses, so the winner is whoever best balances multiple scoring engines rather than maxing one.
